sources.title: Introducing ChatGPT
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The November 30, 2022 launch explicitly says ChatGPT was fine-tuned from a model in the GPT-3.5 series that finished training in early 2022, and calls InstructGPT a sibling. It gives neither a nominal total/active count nor an individually named, sized base checkpoint.

sources.title: InstructGPT Model Card
sources.evidence: Rechecked the raw OpenAI model card October 27, 2026. The January 2022 card names InstructGPT sizes of 1.3B, 6B and 175B and identifies them as GPT-3 fine-tunes. These are nominal specifications for the sibling models; the card does not identify the original ChatGPT checkpoint as one of them.

sources.title: GPT-4 Technical Report
sources.evidence: Re-read the freshly fetched full report October 27, 2026. Figure 6 compares three earlier ChatGPT versions based on GPT-3.5, while Appendix A.7 identifies a standard ChatGPT snapshot without a November 2022 checkpoint identifier. Its comparison tables provide no total or activated-parameter count for the original preview.

sources.title: Introducing APIs for GPT-3.5 Turbo and Whisper
sources.evidence: The API launch identifies gpt-3.5-turbo as the ChatGPT product model at that later release and introduces gpt-3.5-turbo-0301. It explicitly describes ongoing ChatGPT improvements. It supplies no binding to the original November 2022 checkpoint; the page was subsequently updated April 24, 2024.

sources.title: ChatGPT plugins
sources.evidence: March 23, 2023 announcement introduces initial plugin support, including browsing and code execution. Later product tools do not establish an original November 2022 model function-calling interface.

sources.title: Introducing gpt-oss
sources.evidence: OpenAI states in its August 2025 announcement that gpt-oss are its first open-weight language models since GPT-2. This corroborates that the intervening original ChatGPT preview was not an open-weight release.

sources.title: Terms of Use, effective January 1, 2026
sources.evidence: The current terms identify ChatGPT as an OpenAI service, reserve service IP rights and restrict copying or reverse engineering underlying models. Used only to corroborate the descriptive proprietary classification, not to assert that these exact terms applied in November 2022.

sources.title: Archived OpenAI model index for researchers, January 8, 2023
sources.evidence: The prior review received only an archived JavaScript application shell. Reopening the original launch-linked model-index URL and this archived URL on October 27, 2026 failed in the web tool; historical contents still could not be verified. This inaccessible source does not support a count.

sources.title: Does ChatGPT remember what happened earlier in the conversation? December 6, 2022 archive
sources.publisher: OpenAI Help Center, archived by Internet Archive
sources.evidence: The early help page says ChatGPT can reference approximately 3000 words or 4000 tokens from the current conversation. It describes approximate retained conversation history, not an exact combined input/output token budget. The original live URL now returns 404.

sources.title: How People Use ChatGPT
sources.evidence: September 15, 2025 paper, rechecked October 27, 2026. Section 2 describes changing underlying models and weight updates. Appendix C identifies the November 30, 2022 research preview only as using GPT-3.5; it supplies no sized base checkpoint, nominal total, or active count for that release.

sources.title: ChatGPT release notes: December 2022-February 2023 entries
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The December 15, 2022 entry names an updated ChatGPT Dec 15 Version; January entries describe further model upgrades; February 9 and 13 distinguish standard and Turbo versions. These contemporaneous entries confirm changing versions but publish no parameter counts or fixed-size lineage for the November launch.

sources.title: gpt-oss-120b & gpt-oss-20b Model Card
sources.evidence: August 5, 2025 card, rechecked October 27, 2026, including the freshly fetched PDF Table 1 and comparisons. Its explicit total/active parameter table describes only gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b; it supplies no historical ChatGPT count. Targeted searches for ChatGPT active/activated-parameter comparisons found no original November 2022 model row.

sources.title: Language models are few-shot learners
sources.evidence: May 28, 2020 release, reopened October 27, 2026, explicitly specifies GPT-3 at a nominal 175 billion parameters. It does not name the later GPT-3.5 base used for ChatGPT. The ChatGPT launch supplies no unchanged-model relationship to this sized GPT-3 checkpoint, so the 175B count is not transferred.

name.note: ChatGPT is the official name; the parenthetical distinguishes this historical release.

family.note: The training section explicitly identifies GPT-3.5 lineage.

release_date.note: Explicit date of the public research preview.

open_weights.note: Hosted release; later first-party release history confirms weights were not opened.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted, non-open-weight model; not a named checkpoint license or a claim about the exact historical service terms.

parameters_b.note: Fresh primary-source review found no nominal total for the November 2022 preview and no explicit link to a sized base checkpoint. The launch establishes GPT-3.5-series fine-tuning, not identity with GPT-3 175B or any sized InstructGPT variant. Later Turbo and ChatGPT revisions are not substituted. This is a missing published-size link, not a requirement for an exact tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Checked original launch, GPT-4 comparison tables, later OpenAI history and an explicit later active-parameter table; none reports a nominal activated count for the November 2022 preview. Targeted comparison searches produced no exactly identified original-model count. Do not equate a presumed dense total, GPT-3 size, or later ChatGPT version with this value.

architecture.note: Targeted first-party training and interpretability searches did not establish the original checkpoint architecture. InstructGPT card details describe a sibling. The later report distinguishes multiple ChatGPT revisions; legacy documentation was inaccessible beyond its application shell.

context_window.note: The December 2022 FAQ gives approximately 4000 tokens of conversation retention, not an exact context budget. Retain null rather than infer 4096 or substitute later Turbo limits.

modalities.note: The original preview is documented through text dialogue, prompts and responses.

reasoning.note: No dedicated reasoning mode is identified for the original checkpoint. General reasoning examples or later benchmark performance do not establish this feature flag.

tool_call.note: Later plugins and API interfaces do not establish native structured tool calling for the original preview. Absence of an original specification is not proof of incapability.

description.value: Original ChatGPT research preview, fine-tuned from GPT-3.5 using supervised dialogue training and reinforcement learning from human feedback.
description.note: Training summary follows the original Methods section without importing later product features.

patch.description: Original ChatGPT research preview, fine-tuned from GPT-3.5 using supervised dialogue training and reinforcement learning from human feedback.
patch.notes: Historical November 2022 research preview, not a callable API model ID. A December 2022 OpenAI FAQ described approximately 4000 tokens of retained conversation history; an exact context budget was not verified. GPT-3.5-series lineage does not identify a sized base checkpoint; total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed. Architecture is not inferred from InstructGPT or later GPT-3.5 Turbo versions.

summary: Fresh parameter re-audit reopened the original launch, InstructGPT card, GPT-4 report and later Turbo launch, and checked later OpenAI model history and active-count evidence. No nominal total or active parameter count was established for the November 2022 preview: GPT-3.5-series fine-tuning does not identify a sized base, and sibling or later model counts cannot fill that gap. Both parameter fields are explicitly patched to null; the other 12 assessments are unchanged.
